$comment: The walkthrough-generation step is split into the smallest units that can be built and judged on their own. Each piece has: the knobs a builder tunes, the rubric a harsh critic scores it against the reference bar, and live gauntlet state. The gauntlet loops a piece until the critic picks OURS blind, or stops after 3 consecutive non-improving rounds and flags it. Nothing here runs generation by itself; the orchestrator (src/gauntlet.js) drives it once assets are present.

bar.note: Critic must OPEN these directly every round and compare blind (labels stripped), never against a description of them.

flagRule.action: Stop looping this piece, flag to human with current render + named remaining gap, move on. Do not loop forever.

pieces.title: Camera motion
pieces.judged: Smoothness, speed, and a natural path through a room. No warping, no rubber-banding, no jitter, no drift/parallax artifacts on furniture edges.

knobs.model: higgsfield video model + motion params chosen per shot in shot-plan

rubric: Motion reads as a Steadicam/gimbal operator, not a drone lurch or a zoom.
Constant velocity through the middle of the move; gentle ease-in/ease-out at ends.
Straight lines (door frames, counters, ceilings) stay straight through the whole clip.
No morphing of fixtures, no melting reflections, no impossible geometry.

pieces.title: Room-to-room transitions
pieces.judged: How one room hands off to the next: cut rhythm, match-cut alignment, no jarring exposure/scale pops across the boundary.
rubric: Transitions feel intentional and invisible, like a tour editor cut them.
No black flash, no double-exposure mush, no mismatched motion direction across the cut.
Through-doorway moves continue motion direction into the next room.

pieces.title: Framing & composition per shot
pieces.judged: Each shot's start framing: level horizon, leading lines, headroom, hero feature centered, nothing awkwardly cropped.
rubric: Horizon dead level; verticals vertical.
Room's best feature (island, fireplace, view, staircase) anchors the frame.
No clipped ceilings/floors, no dead center-punch when a rule-of-thirds read is stronger.

pieces.title: Pacing against clip length
pieces.judged: Per-shot hold time vs. how much the shot reveals; overall rhythm not too fast (frantic) or too slow (open-house-bored).
rubric: Hero rooms get more time; utility rooms move on quickly.
Cuts land on motion settle, not mid-lurch.
Total length scales with property size (see assembly rubric).

pieces.title: Lighting & color consistency across clips
pieces.judged: Every clip looks shot on the same camera on the same day: consistent white balance, exposure, contrast, and skin/wood/marble tones.

knobs.referenceClip: index of the clip whose grade is the anchor

rubric: No clip is visibly warmer/cooler or brighter/darker than its neighbors.
Whites (marble, cabinetry) read the same white across rooms.
Highlights not blown, shadows not crushed.

pieces.title: Caption / lower-third treatment
pieces.judged: Room labels / feature call-outs: legible, tasteful, on-brand, never covering the hero feature, clean fade timing.
rubric: Looks like a high-end listing brand, not stock TV chyron.
Text inside title-safe margins; never over the subject.
Fades in/out smoothly, matched to the shot's hold.

pieces.title: Final assembly
pieces.judged: The whole video: cut rhythm end-to-end, sequence logic (arrive -> public rooms -> private -> exterior), total length appropriate to property size, optional music bed.
rubric: Plays like a professional property film an agent would send a high-end client.
Flows in a sensible tour order; no whiplash between distant rooms.
Ends on a strong exterior/hero beat; length fits the home's size.
